criteria.text: Each waiting job keeps one ticket in oldest-first order for the next free local slot.
While I wait, pdd reports the local busy count, limit and number ahead of me.
Interruption or the caller deadline removes my waiting ticket without submitting its job.
A waiting ticket or claim abandoned for 60 seconds cannot block my turn when its process ID has been reused.
Only the first waiting ticket competes for a free slot; twelve contenders with three slots make progress without a contention stall.

cases.given: tickets created at 10,20,30; one slot frees
cases.required_observation: 10 acquires, then 20, then 30; one ticket each

cases.given: two tickets share timestamp; reversed directory enumeration
4 occupied slots, limit 4, two older live tickets
cases.required_observation: stderr reports 4 busy/of 4 and 2 ahead; JSON stdout stays valid

cases.given: oldest PID dead; later live waiter
cases.required_observation: dead waiting ticket removed; next live ticket eligible

cases.given: deadline/interrupt before claim and before POST
oldest ticket, separately abandoned claim, has file refresh age 59999 then 60000 ms and a PID now belonging to an unrelated long-lived process
cases.required_observation: fresh case still owns its place/claim; at 60000 ms stale ownership is removed safely and next live waiter can acquire; no successor claim is deleted

cases.given: three ordered tickets, occupied limit, claim contention and injected random values 0 and just below 1
cases.required_observation: only current head attempts acquisition claim; followers wait longer; repeated failures retain original ticket/time; retry delays are positive, bounded, varied by jitter and clipped to deadline

cases.given: 12 separate native processes launched together, shared limit 3, each holds its slot for 20 ms, existing native fixture limit 15 seconds
cases.required_observation: all 12 finish comfortably before the 15-second fixture timeout, measured peak active <=3, no busy failures or duplicated tickets; performance bound belongs to this controlled fixture, not a production hardware SLA
